bug_semantics: In tcprewrite's --fixlen pad path, tcpedit_packet derives ip_hdr/ip6_hdr pointers into the packet buffer and then calls untrunc_packet. The added safe_realloc can move the buffer and free the allocation those derived pointers address; execution then continues to rewrite headers and, for IPv4, fix_ipv4_checksums dereferences the stale ip_hdr. A crafted truncated IPv4 capture therefore causes a heap use-after-free (the reporter's AddressSanitizer trace shows the realloc/free in untrunc_packet and the later read in fix_ipv4_checksums).
flaw_origin: Commit 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 tried to prevent the existing --fixlen pad out-of-bounds memset by changing untrunc_packet to accept u_char ** and inserting packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len), but it neither rebased the already-derived IP header pointers nor, in that commit's tree, assigned the moved packet back through *pktdata before returning. This is the first commit to introduce a realloc/free between header derivation and subsequent header/checksum use. The later 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 only increased that already-vulnerable allocation by PACKET_HEADROOM and is not the BIC.
ai_marker: absent — the raw commit object for 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 has author Fred Klassen <fklassen@appneta.com>, committer Fred Klassen <fklassen@appneta.com>, and only the message 'remalloc packets before padding to ensure not overwriting memory - closes #80'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-assistant trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party disclosure: https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/970 identifies src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c, reports the --fixlen pad reproducer, and gives an AddressSanitizer allocation/free stack in untrunc_packet followed by the stale IPv4-header read in fix_ipv4_checksums; https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9v49-c9x8-3hm2 identifies CVE-2025-9157 and affected versions through 4.5.2-beta2. Origin search: `git log --all --full-history --reverse -S'packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len);' -- src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c` returns 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 as the addition and 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 as the later size-expression replacement; a separate pickaxe for the PACKET_HEADROOM expression returns only 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 and its removal by the fix. BIC source: 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 adds `packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len)` at src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:275 after header pointers have been derived; src/common/utils.c:67-77 shows safe_realloc calls libc realloc. In the same tree src/tcpedit/tcpedit.c:225-228 calls untrunc_packet with the derived ip_hdr/ip6_hdr and lines 231-293 subsequently reuse those pointers, including fix_ipv4_checksums at line 290. Direct-parent proof: `git show 16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e:src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c` shows the pad branch directly calling memset on pktdata and contains no safe_realloc, while the BIC diff replaces that line with the realloc plus memset and changes the API/caller; thus the realloc-driven UAF lines are absent from the one direct parent (although that parent had the distinct overwrite bug the BIC intended to repair). The BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a merge/squash aggregate. Version boundaries: v4.0.4 does not contain the BIC; `git for-each-ref --contains=69831b... refs/tags` begins at v4.0.5beta1 (d0676bfe5f2bddc73a60e9a01a89eeeb2de01eab). v4.5.2-beta2 resolves to 61dd7853b54baa436fbd458e8bfd93d2bdbb00a9, contains the BIC, and does not contain the fix (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 1 for fix -> v4.5.2-beta2). Fix evidence: https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/commit/73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da is direct commit 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da (parent a1778a25a2f8dc4de879782567abab6b923e9694); it removes safe_realloc from src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:574-576, adds a pkthdr.len > MAX_SNAPLEN guard in src/tcprewrite.c, bumps configure.ac from 4.5.2-beta2 to 4.5.2-beta3, and records #970 in docs/CHANGELOG. `git tag --contains 73008f...` starts at v4.5.2; that tag resolves to 98169912173986cc48a4ad325997dcc20c38af28 and contains the fix, matching the advisory's last-affected 4.5.2-beta2 boundary. AI check: `git cat-file -p 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14` yields the exact human author/committer and trailer-free message quoted in ai_marker.
reasoning: The first-party report establishes the vulnerable data flow: a truncated IPv4 packet reaches untrunc_packet through --fixlen pad, realloc may free/move the packet, and checksum calculation later reads a header pointer into the freed allocation. History then distinguishes the true origin from a tempting 2020 blame result: 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 merely changed the reallocation size, whereas 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 first inserted any realloc into this path. Its direct parent 16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e has no realloc, so this specific UAF mechanism is parent-absent. The BIC predates the first containing tag v4.0.5beta1 and remains in the advisory's last vulnerable tag v4.5.2-beta2. Fix 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da removes the unnecessary realloc and bounds declared length to the already-allocated packet capacity; it is absent from v4.5.2-beta2 and present in v4.5.2. Finally, attribution is based only on the BIC's raw commit object: it identifies Fred Klassen as both author and committer and contains no AI/bot marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
